clue.text: It's played with crafty leg-spin that takes Alton in

indicators.note: with in later in the clue, takes in says the shuffled letters swallow another piece
completes takes in: the scrambled bowling term holds the novel's hero within it
crafty spin is artful and twisty, so the letters of leg-spin are turned into a new order

parts.note: Alton Locke is the title hero of Charles Kingsley's novel, so Alton stands for his surname

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a wily spin bowler who deceives a batsman called Alton.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg-spin is a cricket bowling style; 'crafty' scrambles it and 'takes ... in' wraps it round the surname of Kingsley's hero Alton Locke, so 'Alton' gives his other name.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument of tuned metal bars is something one plays with hammers.

clue.text: Bound in triumph, with a Jabberwock's head

definitions.text: Bound in triumph, with a Jabberwock's head

parts.words: Bound in triumph, with a Jabberwock's head
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's poem the hero slays the Jabberwock and goes bounding back home with its head

explanation.definitionFit: Carroll coined this verb for moving in a heavy, triumphant, bounding way, as the hero does after the kill.

clue.text: Instrument decapitates a Welsh buccaneer

indicators.note: cutting off the head removes the first letter of the pirate's name

parts.note: Sir Henry Morgan was a famous Welsh privateer

explanation.surface: A tool is used to behead a Welsh pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe organ is a musical instrument, as found in churches.

clue.text: Jowett, master of Balliol, knew it all

definitions.text: Jowett, master of Balliol, knew it all

parts.words: Jowett, master of Balliol, knew it all
parts.note: recalls the Oxford rhyme about Benjamin Jowett: what I don't know isn't worth knowing, as he claims

explanation.definitionFit: The famous rhyme has Jowett say that whatever he does not know is not learning at all, so he possessed all learning.

clue.text: Simple, elegant and without splash

definitions.meaning: a spirit taken without a splash of water or mixer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means plain, trim and tidy, and also describes undiluted spirits served without water.

clue.text: Wage lists for election procedures round a Scottish burgh

indicators.note: the votes go around the town, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: polls are the votings at elections
Ayr is a town on Scotland's west coast

explanation.surface: Wage records are needed for voting arrangements across a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the Scottish town inside the election word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These are an employer's records of staff and the sums owed to them.

clue.text: Agree to differ? What a bore!

indicators.note: letters that differ from the original are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Agreeing to differ is a tedious way to end an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore here is a tidal wave surging up a river, not a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tidal bore, the surge wave running up an estuary such as the Severn or Trent.

clue.text: Approval won't be slow, the actor hopes

definitions.text: Approval won't be slow, the actor hopes

parts.words: Approval won't be slow, the actor hopes
parts.note: a slow clap from an audience signals impatience, so the actor hopes the applause is brisk

explanation.definitionFit: A slow version of this applause means boredom, so a performer hopes theirs comes quickly as praise.

clue.text: Description Pravda would rightly find infuriating

definitions.text: Description Pravda would rightly find infuriating

parts.words: Description Pravda would rightly find infuriating
parts.note: Pravda was a communist newspaper, literally a ..., and a ... proverbially enrages a bull

explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet paper was a communist journal, a red rag, the phrase for something provoking fury.

clue.text: Roman soldier — or British ex-soldier ?

definitions.meaning: a soldier serving in one of Rome's legions
a member of the Royal British Legion, the veterans' organisation

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a fighter in an ancient Roman legion and a member of the Royal British Legion, the old soldiers' association.

clue.text: Lucy's in hers. Oh, the difference to Wordsworth!

definitions.text: Lucy's in hers. Oh, the difference to Wordsworth!

parts.words: Lucy's in hers. Oh, the difference to Wordsworth!
parts.note: paraphrases the close of Wordsworth's Lucy poem, where the dead girl lies in her burial place and the poet laments the difference to him

explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's poem ends with Lucy in her tomb, the place of burial that changed everything for him.

clue.text: Mutilate many fish

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword stand-in for many
to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: Someone hacks apart a large catch of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutilate is to disfigure or tear apart badly, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Rocky height a nymph enters to find Escamillo

indicators.note: the nymph goes into the hill, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor
an oread is a mountain nymph of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A nymph climbs into a craggy hilltop to look for someone called Escamillo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' sends the mountain nymph into the hill, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo is the bullfighter in Bizet's opera Carmen, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Rhoda's wrecked the stores "

indicators.note: wrecked letters are smashed up and put back together in another order

explanation.surface: Rhoda has trashed the shop's storerooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Stores and hoards are both stockpiles of goods kept for later, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Hang play — change to relief work

indicators.note: the letters are changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A hanging is staged in a play, then switched for some charity work.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a carving or ornament in low relief, a piece of relief sculpture.

clue.text: He works ceaselessly to be a member of the jet set

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A tireless worker hopes to join the glamorous international jet set.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker keeps on working through a strike: a strikebreaker, contemptuously called this in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker carries on working when colleagues down tools, hence the description.

clue.text: Liqueur goes to engineer in unusual auction

indicators.note: the engineers go inside the shuffled letters
unusual signals the letters of auction take an odd order

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A bottle of liqueur is sold to an engineer at a strange auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of auction to COINTAU, and 'in' puts the Royal Engineers among them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a French orange-flavoured spirit, a branded example of the drink.

clue.text: Top people can be so obliging !

definitions.text: Top people can be so obliging

parts.words: Top people can be so obliging
parts.note: refers to the French phrase meaning nobility obliges, the duty of aristocrats

explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for the nobility, the top class whose rank imposes obligations.

clue.text: With tea Argentine VIP has a gooseberry perhaps

parts.note: cha is an old slang word for tea
Juan Peron, the Argentine president

explanation.surface: An important Argentine visitor takes tea with an unwanted third party in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: A gooseberry is British slang for an unwanted third person tagging along with a couple, as a chaperone does.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies a courting pair, playing the role of the unwanted third wheel.

clue.text: Capital of China open yet secret

indicators.note: the capital, or initial letter, of the word China

parts.note: overt means open and unconcealed

explanation.surface: China's capital looks open but hides secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert means hidden or concealed, the opposite of done in the open.

clue.text: Allow one member to enter -the one that's so tenacious

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for allow, one inside the other

parts.note: to allow is to let
I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A club lets in a new member who then clings on stubbornly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts the numeral and the parliamentarian inside the word for allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock-clinging shellfish proverbially grips hard, so it is the type of something tenacious.

clue.text: Strange, in rent revision — but such is Mr Walker's way

indicators.note: strange goes inside the revised word for rent
a revision rewrites the letters into a new order

parts.note: odd means strange

explanation.surface: A tenant finds a strange rent review, but a walker just keeps on going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges the letters of rent to TREN, and 'in' puts the word for strange inside. Johnnie Walker whisky's slogan made Mr Walker a famous striding figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker's path is well-worn and walked on.

clue.text: Little Sarah can be $0 changeable

definitions.meaning: Sal, short for Sarah, followed by this word gives sal ..., smelling salts
liable to change suddenly and unpredictably

explanation.definitionFit: Sal volatile is the old name for smelling salts, and the second word on its own means unstable or fickle.

clue.text: Rugby — score possible ? could be a swindle

parts.note: a try is the main score in rugby
on means possible or feasible, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a rugby score is possible, or whether the match is fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky attempt to deceive someone is British slang for a con.

clue.text: This goes to the wall, reductions being backed by the colonel

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: reductions are cuts
CO is a commanding officer, such as a colonel in charge of a regiment

explanation.surface: A colonel supports budget cuts that will drive a business to the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being backed' turns CUTS into STUC. 'Goes to the wall' usually means fails, but here plaster literally goes on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: This plaster is applied as a coating to walls of buildings.

clue.text: Wendy's nouveau riche papa?

indicators.note: nouveau is French for new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wendy's father has suddenly become vulgarly rich.
explanation.walkthrough: In Peter Pan, Wendy's father is Mr Darling; the French word for darling is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word means darling, and Darling is the surname of Wendy's papa in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Operatic heroine was frigid in the extreme

definitions.text: Operatic heroine was frigid in the extreme

parts.words: Operatic heroine was frigid in the extreme
parts.note: in La Boheme the heroine's tiny hand is frozen, as Rodolfo sings

explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's seamstress in La Boheme famously has a frozen little hand, cold at her extremity.

clue.text: Give back material ? Yes

parts.note: rep is a corded fabric used for upholstery
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should return the cloth, and the answer is yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To give back money or a favour is to reimburse or return it.

clue.text: Employed by Circe to tend her guests ?

definitions.text: Employed by Circe to tend her guests

parts.words: Employed by Circe to tend her guests
parts.note: in the Odyssey the sorceress Circe turns Odysseus's men into pigs, so her guests would need a pig-keeper

explanation.definitionFit: Circe's visitors became hogs, so the one minding them would be a keeper of pigs.

clue.text: As old as Methuselah

parts.note: Methuselah lived before Noah's Flood, so anything that old dates from before the Deluge

explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means before the Flood, and Methuselah is the Bible's pre-Flood ancient, hence very old.
